explanation: The main character in the book of Joshua and leader of the people of Israel after Moses' death.
A holy chest containing the stone tablets with the Ten Commandments, symbolizing God's presence among the people of Israel.
A river in the Middle East that Joshua and the people of Israel cross on their way to the promised land of Canaan.
The promised land that God gives to the people of Israel, described as a land flowing with milk and honey.
The twelve groups of the people of Israel, each tribe being descendants of one of Jacob's sons.
Twelve stones taken from the Jordan River as a memorial to the miracle when God stopped the water so that the people could cross the river.
The place where the Israelites camped after crossing the Jordan River and where they set up a monument with the twelve stones.
A religious ritual in which the foreskin of the penis is removed as a sign of the covenant between God and the people of Israel.
A Jewish festival celebrating the deliverance of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt.
A city in Canaan that was conquered by Joshua and the Israelites through God's help.
